entradas.text: The door swung open and Lucian Galade, my chief strategist, walked in. He was a compact man with sharp, birdlike features. After briefly surveying the room from wall to wall, he sat down, poured a glass of water and opened his briefcase in a series of quick, graceful movements.
Petr Vectern arrived a couple of minutes early and sat across from me. He was struggling to hold back his smile.
“But, hey, back in university, did you ever imagine we would be sitting here in the Maroon Palace? We have to celebrate this great victory.”
“This is not the time to celebrate, Petr. We have work to do.”
entradas.menu: “This is not the time to celebrate, Petr. We have work to do.”

entradas.text: “We will celebrate at the inaugural ball. Just hang in there until the evening.”
entradas.menu: “We will celebrate at the inaugural ball. Just hang in there until the evening.”

entradas.text: “Let's celebrate then. I got my hands on something special for us. An Erlory Maroon 30-year-old.”
entradas.menu: “Let's celebrate then. I got my hands on something special for us. An Erlory Maroon 30-year-old.”

entradas.text: “Looking forward to it. Evelyn hopes to congratulate you in person there.”
“Good to know. It's been some time since the last time I saw her."
entradas.menu: “Good to know. It's been some time since the last time I saw her."

entradas.text: “I'm sure the kids would love to see their Uncle Petr for the first time as the Vice President.”
entradas.menu: “I'm sure the kids would love to see their Uncle Petr for the first time as the Vice President.”

entradas.text: “I think it was Franc's birthday. We've barely had enough time for our families over these past months, haven't we?”
“That is great to hear! It's crazy how fast the two have grown up. You are a good father.”

Petr had a wistful look in his eyes. He and Evelyn had never been able to have kids of their own. During our campaign, the opposition had floated the rumor that he'd fathered illegitimate children during his wilder years, but it had never been substantiated.
“Yes... I agree. We've got things to do today. We can let loose at the ball.”
“Gentlemen.”
“We'll be talking about our political strategy for this term. Lucian and I had a meeting with the party and the reformists."
“We mostly see eye to eye, but I would want to know what you think.”
“Let's see if I see eye to eye.”
entradas.menu: “Let's see if I see eye to eye.”

entradas.text: “Great. Let's go over this when Lucian arrives.”
entradas.menu: “Great. Let's go over this when Lucian arrives.”

entradas.text: The tall-case clock in the room struck three o'clock.
“Hello, Petr.”
“Damn. You are exactly on time."
Lucian then turned towards me. He very slightly bowed his head.

“Another important point. We must be aware of the Lotherberg Group. The Oligarchs convene under this organization to influence economic policies. Konrath Koronti led it for a long time before falling ill. The new leader is Mr. Walter Tusk."
“As far as I know, Konrath's son Marcel has strong ties to this group. His influence could definitely be an asset for us. But I'm sure he'll want something in return."
“I am aware of Mr. Koronti's wide network. That could come in handy.”
entradas.menu: “I am aware of Mr. Koronti's wide network. That could come in handy.”

entradas.text: “The Group's influence is an important force. One that we should use to our administration's advantage.”
entradas.menu: “The Group's influence is an important force. One that we should use to our administration's advantage.”

entradas.text: “That group is dependent on our economic policies. They can't move a finger without us.”
entradas.menu: “That group is dependent on our economic policies. They can't move a finger without us.”

entradas.text: “I wouldn't be so optimistic. The capital they represent could do a lot of damage if it was diverted.”
Lucian took notes.
“We'll see each other at the ball, then."
entradas.menu: “We'll see each other at the ball, then."

entradas.text: “Definitely!"
"Let's move on with the meeting ."
“I hope things are looking good.”
entradas.menu: “I hope things are looking good.”

entradas.text: “According to reports, some members of the National Business Council are in their pockets. Tusk and the Group will surely try to bribe us in exchange for special economic protections.”
Lucian looked at Petr.
“If we can get them to side with us. It all depends on what benefits we can offer and what the leader wants."
“We just need to be careful with him. He looks like the lesser evil, but it could very quickly turn out to be the other way around.”
“We need to tread carefully on all sides with all power players to survive our term. I need to underline the seriousness of the situation.”
“This concludes our political briefing for today. Our next meeting will be about our media strategy.”
Lucian and Petr bid their farewells and left. A mysterious amount of smoke was rising far away on the horizon.
“Let's start by evaluating our current situation."
“It may create issues for us, yes."
“However, with the reformists gaining more popularity, we may not be in a position to stand against them."
“The majority of the Sordish people demand change. They are more concerned about the economy than the Constitution, but they blame the system for their problems."
“It will not be easy."
"People are losing their trust in our democracy. Why do you think radicals like Bernard Circas are becoming more popular? Everyone's expecting us to bring the change the last government did not."
“I agree with the reformists. Our responsibility is to democratize our broken system."
entradas.menu: “I agree with the reformists. Our responsibility is to democratize our broken system."

entradas.text: “We need to listen to the people if we want to serve this country."
entradas.menu: “We need to listen to the people if we want to serve this country."

entradas.text: “We will need many allies against the Old Guard in the government."
“If we lose power, we won't be able to execute the changes we need to make for the good of the country."
entradas.menu: “If we lose power, we won't be able to execute the changes we need to make for the good of the country."

entradas.text: "That's exactly what we campaigned for. A true change that will move the country forward."
“Lucian. How are you?”
entradas.menu: “Lucian. How are you?”

entradas.text: “Glad to see you, Lucian.”
entradas.menu: “Glad to see you, Lucian.”

entradas.text: “Let's not waste any time. Lucian, go ahead with the overview.”
entradas.menu: “Let's not waste any time. Lucian, proceed with the overview.”

entradas.text: “It is a privilege to be here, sir."
“I am ready and able, sir."
“As you wish, sir."
“A comprehensive reform that would make the reformists happy would mean maintaining a balance between all branches of government."
"I agree. The Old Guard won't like this, though."
"We need to work with the Supreme Court one way or the other."
“Which means removing your absolute veto as well. The reformists demand that all loopholes in the Constitution are closed."
“We'll need a comprehensive bill to balance the power structure more fairly."
entradas.menu: “We'll need a comprehensive bill to balance the power structure more fairly."

entradas.text: “The Old Guard will do its best to preserve the Constitution. Chief Justice Hawker and his allied judges have a great influence over the Supreme Court, which will be tough to break."
“Mr. Ricter managed to persuade many members of Assembly to give their support for drafting a new Constitution. Reformist politicians are quickly increasing in number."
"The Court also has the final say over constitutional legislation. Without their approval, we cannot even change it."
“While the reformist wing inside our party is still a minority, they could have a tri-partisan majority in the assembly, especially if they unite under Frens Ricter."
“I agree. They have too much power over Sordish politics."
“We must break the power of the Supreme Court one way or another."
entradas.menu: “We must break the power of the Supreme Court one way or another."

entradas.text: "The reformists' demands are clear. They want to limit the President's veto powers, ensure that the Supreme Court is independent and take away the Court's right to vote on constitutional amendments."
“I support the reformists. We need a proper balance of power in this country."
entradas.menu: “I support the reformists. We need a proper balance of power in this country."

entradas.text: “I'd rather not go against them. The risks are too high."
entradas.menu: “I'd rather not go against them. The risks are too high."

entradas.text: “I agree, sir."
“True. But we can't let the Old Guard manipulate us and then backstab us, like they did with Alphonso."
“We must listen to their demands. Otherwise we are no different than the previous administrations."
entradas.menu: “We must listen to their demands. Otherwise we are no different than the previous administrations."

entradas.text: "I won't allow them to influence me. We will shape our own future."
entradas.menu: "I won't allow them to influence me. We will shape our own future."

entradas.text: "We need to take away their vote in constitutional legislation. It is absurd that they get to vote for bills when they aren't even elected."
"I agree. We can't ignore the winds of change, after all."
“We can figure it out. Our party still holds 130 out of 250 seats in the Assembly. We've got the power."
“We cannot allow obstructionists to exist.”
entradas.menu: “We cannot allow obstructionists to exist.”

entradas.text: “Looks like we have many challenges ahead.”
entradas.menu: “Looks like we have many challenges ahead.”

entradas.text: “We can't underestimate this situation."
entradas.menu: “We can't underestimate this situation."

entradas.text: “We will write a more democratic Constitution with the reformists."
entradas.menu: “We will write a more democratic Constitution with the reformists."

entradas.text: “The new Constitution should give the President wide-ranging powers to lead Sordland into the future."
entradas.menu: “The new Constitution should give the President wide-ranging powers to lead Sordland into the future."

entradas.text: “We could work with the Old Guard to protect our existing extensive powers."
entradas.menu: “We could work with the Old Guard to protect our existing extensive powers."

entradas.text: “How can we come out of this in the best shape?"
entradas.menu: “How can we come out of this in the best shape?"

entradas.text: "That's what we've been preparing for internally. Don't forget that promise is what got us elected."
"The key thing here will be strengthening the power of the Assembly, which we already lead with a majority."
“What do you suggest we do, then?"
entradas.menu: “What do you suggest we do, then?"

entradas.text: "It will be tough to persuade our base if we work with Ricter and his band of reformists. But everyone agrees we need a new Constitution."
“Cut it out, you two. Are you with me or not?"
entradas.menu: “Cut it out, you two. Are you with me or not?"

entradas.text: “That will not be accepted by the reformists. This draft has been created with the advice of both our party and PFJP members."
"That's very bold. Then we must start with eliminating the Supreme Court's authority over constitutional legislation and perhaps take their immunity away."
“You would also be burning bridges with the Reformists and the Old Guard."
"Don't forget the reformists want us to address the loopholes in the presidential veto system."
"You must remember that we promised people a democratic Constitution during the elections."
"How? You know the public wants us to enact extensive reforms. And how do we know if the Old Guard would support you?"
Lucian opened his dossier.
"If we go against the demands of the people, the reformists will be furious. It could backfire."
“What do you suggest we do?"
entradas.menu: “What do you suggest we do?"

entradas.text: "I don't think you should take the risk, Mr. President."
“You might be right."
entradas.menu: “You might be right."

entradas.text: “Only a strong administration can make Sordland great."
entradas.menu: “Only a strong administration can make Sordland great."

entradas.text: “I will not limit my veto powers. We need them."
entradas.menu: “I will not limit my veto powers. We need them."

entradas.text: "Very well. We will begin to explore how to realistically pass such a constitutional change."
“They can remain. Some reform is better than none."
entradas.menu: “They can remain. Some reform is better than none."

entradas.text: “As you wish. We will move forward on that."
“Of course, it will be looked at in detail."
entradas.menu: “Of course, it will be looked at in detail."

entradas.text: "That is true, but if we don't evolve we might become part of the problem."
"However, I must stress that I am not for this."
“Yes, sir."
“Second, the President's absolute veto will be taken away. This can be replaced with a limited veto system by fixing the current loopholes."
“We must draft a bill to destroy the power of the judiciary."
entradas.menu: “We must draft a bill to destroy the power of the judiciary."

entradas.text: “Taking away the legislative power of the Supreme Court while holding your own absolute authority over legislation would look like an attempt to consolidate your own power."
"Yes. The divisions of power need to be rebalanced for a better Sordland."
"Fair enough. Let's work with the reformists."
“We can handle it, just like the previous governments did."
entradas.menu: “We can handle it, just like the previous governments did."

entradas.text: “True, we can't do it. It is too dangerous."
entradas.menu: “True, we can't do it. It is too dangerous."

entradas.text: "We must draft a bill with more executive powers."
entradas.menu: "We must draft a bill with more executive powers."

entradas.text: "It is not a risk worth taking, Mr. President."
"No, I will only support a new constitution that strengthens my position. Forget the reformists and reach out to the NFP instead."
"Then I don't intend to pursue constitutional change. We will reach out to the Old Guard."
entradas.menu: "Then I don't intend to pursue constitutional change. We will reach out to the Old Guard."

entradas.text: "It will be a dangerous path to follow."
“I can handle them. It will be done under the Rayne administration."
entradas.menu: “I can handle them. It will be done under the Rayne administration."

entradas.text: "Why would you want to work with the Old Guard?"
“Without the Sollists' support, we have no power."
entradas.menu: “Without the Sollists' support, we have no power."

entradas.text: "Keeping your absolute veto over legislation but taking away the Supreme Court's influence over the Assembly would make it look like a power grab."
“I need to maintain my powers."
entradas.menu: “I need to maintain my powers."

entradas.text: “We can do it, Lucian! Look at what we accomplished so far."
entradas.menu: “We can do it, Lucian! Look at what we accomplished so far."

entradas.text: "The state is powerful as is. The question is how to approach these constitutional amendments and if it's realistic to pull off."
"You're talking about going against the reformists and public opinion all at once."
"Mr. Vice President has a point."
"I understand. We do not have to remove your veto. Instead, we can discuss limiting it with the reformists."
"I don't know if we can survive that politically."
“What do you suggest we do then? Maybe I can reconsider working with the reformists."
"No. This is not happening. I'd rather not include either of these points."
"I want to minimize the damage to my seat."
entradas.menu: "I want to minimize the damage to my seat."

entradas.text: “I have no problems with these clauses. Let's work with the reformists."
entradas.menu: “I have no problems with these clauses. Let's work with the reformists."

entradas.text: "The President needs to be able to exercise his powers with ease to maintain stability."
entradas.menu: "The President needs to be able to exercise his powers with ease to maintain stability."

entradas.text: "We must strengthen the state by removing the power of the Old Guard."
entradas.menu: "We must strengthen the state by removing the power of the Old Guard."

entradas.text: “The real problem is the judiciary's power, not the president's."
entradas.menu: “The real problem is the judiciary's power, not the president's."

entradas.text: "Yes. Of course I'm with you."
“We need to address other more important problems, too."
“What is the best outcome for us then?"
entradas.menu: “What is the best outcome for us then?"

entradas.text: "If you are serious about this, I will explore the options for you, Mr. President."
“To clarify before we head in any particular direction, what are your intentions, sir?"
“The public might be persuaded, but the reformists in the Assembly are not going to fall for that."
“They would try to paint you as yet another strongman trying to grab more power for himself."
“What do you suggest, Lucian?"
entradas.menu: “What do you suggest, Lucian?"

entradas.text: "It would be quite difficult to secure the 166 votes needed to propose such a bill."
“What about you, Petr?"
entradas.menu: “What about you, Petr?"

entradas.text: "It will be very difficult to plead that case to the reformists."
"Anton, we got elected by promising democratic reforms."
“That would be tough, sir. But I trust your judgement."
"We would lose all reformist support."
"That does include strengthening the Assembly by giving them a chance to override vetoes, as well as ensuring that the judiciary is independent."
"We don't need the reformists. We can always work with the NFP."
“As you wish. We will move forward on that."
“We can package it as a *democratic* reform.”
entradas.menu: “We can package it as a *democratic* reform.”

entradas.text: “However, most people will not be persuaded by that. It would be tough to reach the 166 votes needed to propose such a bill."
“You're right. Let's work with the reformists."
“No matter what you say, I intend to come out of this stronger as the President.”
entradas.menu: “No matter what you say, I intend to come out of this stronger as the President.”

entradas.text: "Well... Let's see what we can do about it."
“I somewhat agree with you, sir."
"What everyone's expecting is a rebalance of power between the executive, legislative and judiciary branches."
"Of course. We'll have time to discuss everything you want."
“If it must be done, I will do it."
entradas.menu: “If it must be done, I will do it."

entradas.text: "The reformists are pretty loud about their thoughts on the presidential powers, Anton. You know they think this position breeds dictators."
“Can't we avoid strengthening the Assembly?"
entradas.menu: “Can't we avoid strengthening the Assembly?"

entradas.text: “According to the initial draft we made with the reformists, there are two changes to the Constitution that are not open for their discussion."
“I see that. But we will move towards this direction for now."
entradas.menu: “I see that. But we will move towards this direction for now."

entradas.text: “I don't care what they think. We can handle them."
“First, the Supreme Court will no longer vote on constitutional amendments."
“The entire process will take a long time. But we must start working with a reform committee to evaluate all possibilities for a new Constitution as soon as possible.”
“We will form a reform committee together with all parties and start reaching out to all the stakeholders in the Assembly and the Court for a new Constitution."
“We will form a reform committee and start talking with all stakeholders in the Assembly and the Court to see if such changes to the Constitution would be possible."
“Let us at least work with a reform committee to start talking with all stakeholders in the Assembly and the Court just to query opinions. I'll try to reach out to the Old Guard, in the meantime."
"By later in the year, we should have an idea of the reform contents and what the other parties want."
"By later in the year, we should know more about the reform contents and how to balance the clauses of the new Constitution."
"By later in the year, we should have an idea about the reform contents and what the other parties want. Then we can decide whether to pull the trigger."
“Our party must fall in line with our position. We can't have a strong divide."
entradas.menu: “Our party must fall in line with our position. We can't have a strong divide."

entradas.text: “The USP reformists aren't wrong to agree that we need change, but we should be in charge."
entradas.menu: “The USP reformists aren't wrong to agree that we need change, but we should be in charge."

entradas.text: "We can't let the PFJP leadership take the spotlight on this."
"True. If our party fractures, it's the opposition that will benefit."
“Mr. Ricter could be a potential ally in our goal to maintain a majority in the Assembly."
entradas.menu: “Mr. Ricter could be a potential ally in our goal to maintain a majority in the Assembly."

entradas.text: “He's definitely key in this."
Petr looked troubled.
Lucian raised an eyebrow.
Lucian nodded.
Petr nodded in agreement.
Petr shook his head.
Lucian scratched his head.
“I won't be bought, it won't happen.”
entradas.menu: “I won't be bought, it won't happen.”

entradas.text: “I will enter a dialogue with them eventually. We need to be diplomatic.”
entradas.menu: “I will enter a dialogue with them eventually. We need to be diplomatic.”

entradas.text: “However, to reform the constitution we must receive a two-thirds majority in the Grand National Assembly, which is 166 votes. *And* a simple majority in the Supreme Court that equates to 6 votes.”
“After we have settled on how to proceed, we will need to talk with our party figures. Our first goal must be to get the 150 signatures needed to start the process.”
“Of course."
Lucian looked at his watch.
“Well then, gentlemen. Precisely 30 minutes.”
“Talk to you soon, sir. I will keep in touch.”
“See you both at the next meeting.”
“True. But we can't let the Old Guard manipulate us and then backstab us, like we did with Alphonso."
“Frens Ricter, leader of the reformists, believes that true change can only be accomplished by transferring some of our powers to the Assembly. I will move into the details of their demands shortly."
“We did it Anton, we won! Finally! All those years with our noses to the grindstone paid off."
“Following the greenlight from the USP, we will reach out to the other party leaders to see if they would back our draft. The last step is to convince the justices of the Court.”

Petr's eyes sparkled. The strain of the past months had put a damper on his usual rakish charm, but today he was looking and acting more like his old self. He loosened his tie and undid the top two buttons of his shirt.
"Enjoying the new secretary I picked out for you? Thought you'd appreciate her gorgeous set of... talents. It's a shame the rest of your staff aren't as easy on the eyes."
He gestured to the slight paunch that protruded over his waistband.
Lucian spoke in soft, clipped tones that immediately drew your attention towards what he had to say. Petr and I waited for him to proceed.
“We did it Anton, we won! Finally! The bribery, the backstabbing -- it's all paid off."
“We did it Anton, we won! Finally! All those games we played with the media paid off."

“Our election campaign promised to focus on the military. This was a safe choice. The military and the general staff are a powerful element in the state, and as history tells us, a dangerous one too.”

“The military and the general staff are a powerful element in the state, and as history tells us, a dangerous one too. We do have some room to make structural changes -- by reducing their budget, for example. But it is quite limited."
“I want to work with them anyway. The new administration will be open to talk to businessmen.”
entradas.menu: “I want to work with them anyway. The new administration will be open to talk to businessmen.”

entradas.text: “The military can be close allies. And with the Rumburg threat on the horizon, we need them.”
entradas.menu: “The military can be close allies. And with the Rumburg threat on the horizon, we need them.”

entradas.text: “The Sordish Armed Forces represent our pride as a nation and will be funded as promised.”
entradas.menu: “The Sordish Armed Forces represent our pride as a nation and will be funded as promised.”

entradas.text: “With the Rumburg threat on the horizon, we can't reduce our defense capability and anger our General Staff.”
entradas.menu: “With the Rumburg threat on the horizon, we can't reduce our defense capability and anger our General Staff.”

entradas.text: “The military has been nothing but a burden on our society. We should do something drastic -- like cutting their funding.”
entradas.menu: “The military has been nothing but a burden on our society. We should do something drastic -- like cutting their funding.”

entradas.text: “If they prove to be a political threat in the future, we can get rid of them.”
entradas.menu: “If they prove to be a political threat in the future, we can get rid of them.”

entradas.text: “Rumburg is a massive threat. One that also requires us to ally with other, stronger nations.”
“That will ensure they will be on our side unless we do something drastic in the course of our term.”
“I would advise the same. The budget should be maintained and we should refrain from confronting the military too directly.”
“That is possible, but we can be sure that there will be a strong negative reaction. If we push the military too far, it could cause real trouble.”
“Bold strategy Mr. President. One that could work, but we would need to amend the constitution first. Let's not get ahead of ourselves.”
“If we act strongly against the military, both of those guys will unite against us. I agree with Lucian. We need to tread carefully here."

“Defense Minister Iosef Lancea is more loyal to us compared to General Kruger. A fact that obviously can change with our actions. Either way, I see a potential rift between the two since they are clearly of different minds.”
“None of us want to live through the 1927 scenario again.”
“I don't want to die in prison just like Artor S. Wisci did.”
entradas.menu: “I don't want to die in prison just like Artor S. Wisci did.”

entradas.text: “It is sound to listen to them but they have very biased and narrow opinions. Nationalism clouds their minds. General Kruger is a specter of the past.”
“I want to receive the advice of the military before making up my mind.”
entradas.menu: “I want to receive the advice of the military before making up my mind.”

entradas.text: “We won't let these privileged, greedy, and snobby capitalists run the country.”
entradas.menu: “We won't let these privileged, greedy, and snobby capitalists run the country.”

entradas.text: “It's always easier for the administration to have businesses' support.”
“Alphonso said the same thing. I doubt there was anybody else to turn to in his case.”
“Wise approach. It's good to understand and see if we can reach a middle ground.”
“Let's not underestimate their influence. These are not harmless people either.”
“He'd be a useful ally as well. Tusk has an incredible network and owns a good amount of Bergia Steel.”
“Tusk is heading the group. We should make sure he is on our side.”
entradas.menu: “Tusk is heading the group. We should make sure he is on our side.”

entradas.text: Petr looked troubled.
"That's exactly what I'm aiming to do."
